passages.title: Power from the tides
passages.subtitle: Demo passage
passages.text:
[A] Tidal power uses the regular rise and fall of the sea. Unlike wind or sunshine, tides can be predicted years in advance, which makes the electricity they produce easier to plan around.

[B] The first large tidal barrage began operating in 1966 and still supplies power today. However, barrages can change the habitats of fish and birds living in the estuary, and building one is extremely expensive.

[C] More recent designs place turbines directly on the seabed. These resemble underwater windmills and cause less environmental disruption, but they must survive strong currents and salt water, so maintenance costs remain high.
